sources.title: Zero-shot learning - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Zero-shot learning (ZSL) is a problem setup in machine learning where, at test time, a learner observes samples from classes which were not observed during training, and needs to predict their class. The name is a play on words based on the earlier concept of one-shot learning in computer vision, in which classification can be learned from only one example. sources.title: Zero-Shot vs One-Shot vs Few-Shot Learning - GeeksforGeeks
sources.snippet: In artificial intelligence (AI), zero-shot and few-shot learning are groundbreaking concepts that have significantly advanced the capabilities of machine learning models. These techniques enable models to recognize and classify new data with little or no training examples, making them incredibly versatile and efficient.
